jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
The Challenged Athletes Foundation® (CAF) is a world leader in helping individuals with physical disabilities get involved and stay involved in sports and fitness. CAF believes that participation in sports at any level increases self-esteem, encourages independence, and enhances quality of life. Since 1994, CAF has provided millions of dollars in grants and resources that empower individuals with physical disabilities to pursue active lifestyles through sport. CAF is headquartered in San Diego, California, with additional regional presence across the United States.

Position overview:

The Chief Operating Officer role is a new role to the organization. CAF is looking for a COO to help lead the organization through its next phase of growth and impact. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Director, the COO will serve as a key strategic partner, ensuring alignment between vision, operations, people and performance across the organization. This role requires an experienced leader that can maintain and build upon the culture of the organization while simultaneously guiding the organization through the change management necessary to secure the future of the organization. 

Who we're looking for: 

The right person for this role is highly strategic, financially sophisticated, and they thrive at the intersection of leadership, accountability, and execution. This individual will play a critical role in strengthening organizational performance while helping build a culture where leaders think and operating like true owners of their departments. 

The ideal candidate: 

Possesses exceptional financial acumen and a deep understanding of budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation, performance metrics and financial stewardship.
Has a proven track record of driving organization-wide financial accountability and helping leadership teams make decisions grounded in data, outcomes, and fiscal responsibilities.
Can successfully facilitate a strategic shift in leadership focus toward operational excellence, measurable results, and sustainable financial performance.
Provides support to leaders that allows them to take ownership of their functions, empower department heads to think strategically, manage resources effectively, and operate with an enterprise-wide mindset.
Brings outstanding communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to serve as a trusted bridge between the Board of Directors, executive leadership, and operational teams.
Is comfortable engaging with board members on strategy, organizational performance, financial health, and key business initiatives while translating board priorities into actionable organizational outcomes.
Balances strategic vision with hands-on, execution oriented leadership style.
Is passionate about mission driven work and creating meaningful impact in the community.

Responsibilities: 

Organizational Leadership and Execution: 

In partnership with the Chief Executive Director, this role will translate organizational strategy into actionable operational plans, priorities and performance objectives.
This role will directly support the Chief Accounting Officer, Chief Marketing Officer, Chief Programs Officer and the HR function.
They will assist in establishing department goals that are aligned to the organization priorities.
The COO will remove roadblocks, assist to establish and operationalize plans, and align departmental projects so the team is able to make an impact.

Financial and Operational Stewardship:

In partnership with the Chief Accounting Officer, this role will be engaged in the development, implementation and monitoring of annual budgets.
Maintain accountability for organizational resource allocation, ensuring investments align with strategic priorities and operational requirements.
Monitor department financial performance and recommend corrective actions when performance deviates from budget or plan.
Identify and implement cost effective solutions that improve organizational efficiency while maintaining service quality and mission impact.

Process improvement, Data and Reporting:

Lead organizational process improvement initiatives including workflow redesign, standardization and continuous improvement efforts. Drive technology
Oversee organizational reporting systems and create performance dashboards to ensure timely, accurate and actionable information is available to leadership.
Establish and monitor KPI's and organizational metrics that measure operational, programmatic and financial performance.
Utilize operational and financial data to support strategic planning, decision making, and organizational sustainability.
Drive technology adoption and process integration initiatives

Total Rewards Strategy at CAF: 

CAF offers a competitive compensation package, commensurate with experience. The expected salary range for this position is between $150,000 - $170,000. CAF also offers a complete benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401k match, generous vacation and holiday schedule, hybrid work schedule, onsite weekly team lunches, an engaging culture, and a dog friendly work place. 

Qualifications: 

Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree in Business Administration, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, or related field preferred. 
Minimum of 7-10 years of progressive nonprofit leadership experience.
Demonstrated experience leading operational functions within a nonprofit organization.
Strong financial acumen, including budget development, financial analysis, forecasting, and resource management.
Experience overseeing multiple departments and leading cross-functional teams.
Proven ability to develop strategic plans and translate them into measurable operational outcomes.
Experience utilizing data, reporting, and performance metrics to drive organizational improvement.
Excellent leadership, communication, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
Demonstrated success managing change and improving organizational processes.
Ability to work effectively with executive leadership, board members, staff, volunteers, donors, and community stakeholders.
Commitment to CAF's mission and values.
Willingness to travel and work occasional evenings and weekends as required

jobs.title: Chief Advancement Officer
jobs.description:
Merito Group with headquarters in Oakland, Maryland, is a fast growing woman owned Small Business and HUBZone company with an outstanding record of performance providing more effective and efficient acquisition, business process, training, IT, administrative and security services to multiple federal agencies.

Merito Group is looking for a Chief Advancement Officer to support their client.
Salary range $120,000-$125,000

Chief Advancement Officer

Location: Staten Island NY
Duration: Full Time Direct Hire

Position Summary

The Chief Advancement Officer (CAO)
is a senior philanthropy executive and a key member of the Executive Team, responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive advancement strategy that accelerates philanthropic revenue, diversifies private funding sources, and strengthens the organization's long-term financial sustainability. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the CAO serves as a strategic partner to the CEO and Board of Directors, aligning philanthropy with our mission, strategic priorities, and vision for community impact. The CAO is expected to serve as an enterprise leader, contributing to organizational strategy and acting as a trusted advisor to the CEO on matters of philanthropy, external relations, and long-term organizational sustainability.

The CAO provides executive leadership for all advancement functions, including major gifts, annual and planned giving, foundation and corporate partnerships, donor stewardship, capital and special campaigns, signature fundraising events, and community engagement. The CAO will build and lead a high-performing Advancement team, cultivate transformational relationships with donors and strategic partners, and serve as a visible ambassador for us throughout Staten Island and the greater New York philanthropic community. Through innovation, collaboration, and data-driven decision-making, the CAO will strengthen the organization's brand, expand philanthropic investment, and advance our mission and community impact.

The CAO will lead and develop the Advancement Department, providing direct supervision to the Director of Development and Senior Development Associate while overseeing the work of advancement consultants and external partners, including government relations, fund development, and grant writing. The CAO will ensure that the department's people, systems, and external resources are aligned to achieve our strategic fundraising and philanthropic objectives.

In partnership with the CEO, the CAO serves as the primary staff liaison to the Board of Directors' Development Committee, working closely with the Committee Chair to advance the Board's fundraising priorities, strengthen Board engagement in philanthropy, and support a culture of philanthropy and Board engagement.
As our chief fundraising strategist and ambassador, the CAO will champion innovation, collaboration, and accountability to position the organization for sustained philanthropic growth and lasting community impact.

Executive Leadership

Serve as chief philanthropy executive and strategic advisor to the CEO.
Develop, execute, and continuously refine a comprehensive advancement strategy aligned with the organization's strategic plan and long-term financial goals.
Foster a culture of philanthropy across the organization.
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing Advancement team and oversee external consultants and strategic partners.

Fundraising & Revenue Growth

Lead all philanthropic revenue strategies, including major gifts, annual giving, planned giving, foundation relations, corporate partnerships, campaigns, and donor stewardship.
Expand unrestricted revenue and diversify philanthropic funding sources.
Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward high-capacity donors, foundations, corporations, and strategic partners.
Establish measurable fundraising goals, evaluate organizational performance, and use data to drive continuous improvement.

Board & Executive Partnership

Partner closely with the CEO and Board of Directors to advance fundraising priorities and organizational growth.
Serve as the primary staff liaison to the Board Development Committee and work closely with the Committee Chair to strengthen Board engagement in philanthropy.
Prepare and present fundraising strategies, reports, and recommendations to executive leadership and the Board.

External Relations & Brand Leadership

Represent us with donors, foundations, corporations, elected officials, faith communities, and community leaders.
Strengthen the organization's visibility, reputation, and philanthropic presence throughout Staten Island and the greater New York region.
Provide executive oversight of advancement communications, marketing, and donor engagement initiatives.

Advancement Operations

Ensure best-in-class advancement operations, including CRM management, fundraising analytics, prospect development, stewardship, reporting, and performance measurement.
Build and continuously strengthen the systems, processes, technology, and infrastructure necessary to support sustainable fundraising growth and operational excellence.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred.
Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible leadership in nonprofit fundraising or advancement.
Demonstrated success securing and stewarding five-, six-, and seven-figure gifts.
Proven track record of increasing philanthropic revenue and diversifying funding sources.
Experience leading comprehensive advancement programs and high-performing teams.
Experience partnering effectively with CEOs, Boards of Directors, and executive leadership.
Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and strategic leadership skills.

Preferred

Experience in human services, healthcare, or a mission-driven nonprofit organization.
Experience leading capital campaigns and planned giving programs.
Knowledge of government funding and public-private partnerships.

Why Join US

Our client is Staten Island's leading human services organization, dedicated to ending hunger and homelessness and strengthening communities through compassionate, comprehensive services. The Chief Advancement Officer will have a unique opportunity to shape the organization's philanthropic future, build a best-in-class advancement program, and partner with an engaged CEO, Board of Directors, and Executive Team to expand impact for thousands of individuals and families across the region.

Compensation

The salary range for this position is $120,000-$125,000, commensurate with qualifications and experience. In addition to base salary, the Chief Advancement Officer will be eligible to participate in a performance-based incentive plan tied to the achievement of mutually agreed-upon strategic advancement objectives, organizational growth, and long-term philanthropic sustainability.

jobs.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Executive Director, Technology Product Management – Medical Cost Initiatives

Location:
Remote

Department:
Healthcare Technology & Product Management

Reports To:
VP, Chief Health Informatics Officer (CHIO) - CVS Healthcare Delivery

Role Overview

As the Executive Director, Digital Product – Medical Cost Initiatives
, you will lead the technology product strategy and execution for key medical cost portfolios for CVS Healthcare Delivery businesses. Core areas of focus are Care Transitions, Patient Segmentation, Chronic Condition Pathways, and Specialty Care Services.

In this high-impact executive role, you will partner directly with clinical and business operational leaders to shape end-to-end technology pathways that support CVS Healthcare Delivery care models. You will lead a multidisciplinary team of product managers, Epic analysts, software engineers, data scientists, and UI/UX designers to translate clinical vision into scalable technology roadmaps that optimize patient outcomes and lower the total cost of care.

The ideal candidate must have expertise with value-based care models and Epic as a core care delivery platform.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Business Partnership & Care Model Integration

Partner with healthcare delivery leadership to collaborate on end-to-end care models across transitions, chronic care pathways, patient segmentation, and specialty care.
Serve as a strategic thought partner with CVS HCD business stakeholders as they define the "why" and the "what.’ Serve as the accountable party to ensure cross-functional technology teams deliver meaningful technology solutions to drive core business outcomes.
Establish shared outcome metrics with business leaders, ensuring all technology investments directly drive improved clinical quality, patient experience, and financial performance.

Product & Technology Leadership

Lead multidisciplinary technology teams —including Product Managers, Epic Analysts, Software Engineers, Data Scientists, and Designers—to build seamless, end-to-end clinical technology pathways that reduce medical costs, while driving patient experience and outcomes.
Oversee the transformation of broad clinical ideas into rigorous problem statements, actionable product specifications, and robust Epic/technology architectures.
Ensure smooth integration between external data sources (e.g., claims data, remote monitoring, health plan feeds) and internal Epic workflows to provide clinicians with real-time, actionable insights. Know when these integrations are needed and partner with technical team members to ensure effective execution that works well in clinical practice.

Operational Execution & Continuous Improvement

Take end-to-end accountability for the technology lifecycle, from initial problem discovery through technical solutioning, build, deployment, and measurable outcome realization.
Establish continuous feedback loops and iterative improvement cycles to ensure deployed technologies achieve targeted clinical and financial goals.
Maintain a deep operational understanding of both Value-Based Care (VBC) and Fee-for-Service (FFS) delivery environments to ensure solutions scale across business models.

Team Leadership & Culture

Lead, mentor, and build a high-performing product team of "translators"—professionals fluent in both healthcare operations and technology capability.
Lead and mentor cross-functional technology teams beyond product - Epic analysts, engineers, data scientists - focused on driving success in CVS HCD Medical Cost Initiatives.
Foster a team culture grounded in curiosity, resilience, problem-solving, and joy, maintaining high engagement even during complex, high-pressure execution cycles.

Qualifications & Key Competencies

Executive Presence: Proven ability to communicate, influence, and build trust with senior executive stakeholders and frontline team members alike.
Epic & Healthcare Tech Expertise: Hands-on experience with Epic EHR workflows, module configurations, and translating operational requirements into Epic builds. Understanding of how external health data enriches EHR clinical workflows.
Healthcare Operations & Domain Knowledge: Deep familiarity with clinical operations, Quality Improvement (QI) methodologies, Value-Based Care (VBC) constructs, and Fee-For-Service (FFS) operational dynamics, and medical cost initiative care pathways.
Product & Technical Leadership: Track record of leading cross-functional teams to deliver high-scale technology backed clinical interventions.
Problem-Solving & Accountability: Exceptional analytical rigor; ability to frame ambiguous clinical challenges into structured problem statements and hold teams accountable to measurable outcomes.
Hands-on Leader: Knows when to delegate and work alongside team members to drive success.
People Leadership: Demonstrated ability to lead with empathy, optimism, and rigor, building high-trust teams that excel under pressure.

Required Experience & Education

Education: Bachelor’s degree required; Graduate degree and/or clinical background preferred (RN, MD, DO, NP, PA)
Experience: 10-15+ years of progressive leadership experience spanning healthcare operations, clinical technology product management, and enterprise EHR implementation (specifically Epic).
Track Record: Proven history of partnering with primary care delivery networks, retail clinics, or value-based care organizations to improve medical cost trends and clinical care pathways.

Travel & Location

Domestic travel approximately generally once per quarter, but could be more frequent.
Location remote anywhere in the U.S.

The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

jobs.description:
The UFCW National Health and Welfare Fund, located in Englewood, New Jersey, is seeking an experienced Executive Director to provide strategic, operational, and administrative leadership for a complex multiemployer health and welfare plan serving active members, retirees, beneficiaries, and their eligible dependents. The Fund administers health benefits, including payment of medical and hospital claims, for approximately 8,384 active members and eligible dependents and approximately 463 retirees and beneficiaries. A satellite office is maintained in Stockton, California.

Reporting to and taking direction from the Board of Trustees, the Executive Director translates Trustee initiatives into actionable plans. The successful candidate will bring sound judgment, critical thinking and the ability to navigate complex operational and regulatory issues, while building strong, collaborative relationships with staff, Trustees, unions, employers, and professional advisors in service of the Fund’s participants and beneficiaries. The Executive Director oversees an Associate Executive Director and approximately 30 collectively bargained staff members. This position requires full-time onsite presence and periodic travel.

This role is accountable for the Fund’s overall administrative performance, including day-to-day operations, service delivery, compliance, accuracy, timeliness, and continuous process improvement. The Executive Director leads by setting clear priorities, using data to inform decisions, managing risk proactively, and aligning people, processes, and vendors with Trustee-established goals.

As the senior leader of the Fund Office, the Executive Director helps ensure effective plan implementation, strong compliance, excellent participant service, while fostering a respectful, accountable, and high-performing culture across staff and stakeholders.

Responsibilities

In addition to the above, key goals and responsibilities include:

Own day-to-day operations, set performance standards, align resources, and drive process improvements that support the Fund’s goals.
Lead and develop the staff; build strong working relationships grounded in trust, accountability, and transparent communication.
Deliver accurate, timely, and consistent plan administration and member service, supported by clear performance standards and continuous improvement.
Implement and support multiple health plan design variations negotiated by the Board of Trustees for individual employers or groups of employers.
Support Board of Trustees decision making through clear data analysis, reporting, options, recommendations, and timely communication on project status.
Direct financial stewardship for the Fund’s administrative budget, ensuring strong controls, clear reporting, and transparency.
Provide governance support by coordinating Board and committee agendas and materials, documenting decisions, and ensuring completion of deliverables, including coordinating the completion of all projects as directed by the Board with counsel, other professional advisors and any and all service providers.
Represent the Fund professionally with unions, employers, advisors, vendors, and government agencies as appropriate.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate brings:

10+ years of progressively responsible experience in health plan administration and compliance; 10+ years in senior leadership, including executive-level decision making with Trustees or governing boards.
Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree, such as an MBA, and/or CEBS preferred.
Experience managing collectively bargained staff preferred.
Direct experience with self-administered health plan administration and medical claims operations.
Demonstrated ability to lead staff and build relationships with boards, staff, unions, employers, and external advisors—balancing differing perspectives with professionalism and diplomacy. Experience managing collectively bargained staff a plus.
Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, including the ability to interpret multiple health plan designs and financial, operational, audit, and regulatory information and translate it into clear recommendations or requirements.
Strategic mindset with a commitment to continuous learning and improvement.
Proven ability to take direction and implement initiatives efficiently.
Sound judgment in using available resources effectively and appropriately.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with confidence presenting recommendations, options, tradeoffs, and outcomes to diverse audiences.
Ability to travel up to 25%.

To Apply

In addition to a salary range of $250,000 - $300,000 commensurate with experience, the Fund offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes paid healthcare, defined contribution and defined benefit retirement plans, and generous paid leave. The Fund is an affirmative action employer and encourages applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, race, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, marital status, religion, or disability.

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer - nonprofit
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Few childhood events are as life-altering as the death of a parent, sibling, or significant person. Since 1999, Brooke's Place has helped change the lives of grieving children and families through peer support groups, therapy services, camp-based programming, and community education. With the retirement of a long-time Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Brooke's Place is seeking a mission-centered, people-oriented leader who will preserve the organization's warmth and clinical integrity while preparing it for responsible growth.
Brooke's Place is the only organization providing ongoing grief services specifically for children and families in Central Indiana. Poised for continued growth, we seek an inspiring and experienced leader who can build on a strong foundation of committed donors, volunteers, staff, and community partners. The next CEO will bring strong communication and relationship-building skills, sound business judgment, emotional intelligence, and the ability to translate vision into sustainable results without losing sight of the mission.

What and Who You'll Lead

As CEO, the selected candidate will be responsible for the overall leadership and management of Brooke's Place organization, including but not limited to: community and public relations, fundraising; development and cultivation of donors, program service models and expansion; human resources management, grant-writing oversight; financial management and compliance; Board of Directors administration and support; and legal, tax, risk and facilities management. Three of the 15 staff members report directly to this individual, who reports to the Brooke's Place Board of Directors.

The CEO will partner closely with the Board on strategic direction, fund development, and organizational priorities. Working in partnership with clinical and functional leaders, the CEO will strengthen the people, systems, partnerships, and infrastructure needed to expand impact while protecting program quality and organizational culture.
The role also requires visible and flexible leadership of a mission-driven team whose programs, volunteer activities, donor events, and family needs may extend beyond traditional business hours.

Key Priorities for the First 12 Months

· Build trust with staff, board, donors, and community partners through presence, transparency, and consistent follow-through, establishing relationships with deeply passionate volunteers, staff, and donors.
· Collaborate with the Clinical Programs Director and program team to assess the current state of programs and operations, assessing whether the model is right-sized and right-shaped for current demand, future growth, geographic reach, and long-term organizational sustainability.
· Work with the Advancement Director and team to strengthen financial systems, stewardship practices, and development infrastructure, with meaningful progress toward new major gift relationships, corporate partnerships, planned giving efforts, and a diversified revenue base.
· Evaluate the facilities, technology, data, staffing, and operating capabilities needed for the organization's next phase.
· Deepen referral and community partnerships across schools, healthcare, hospice, funeral service, nonprofit, civic, and business networks.
· Improve the use of outcomes and evaluation to demonstrate impact, inform decisions, and support fundraising.
· Foster a culture in which staff and volunteers feel supported, valued, accountable, and equipped to succeed.

Who We're Looking For

Brooke's Place seeks a leader first, with genuine passion for this mission. The ideal candidate:
· Brings eight to ten or more years of proven senior leadership, preferably in the nonprofit sector (through employment, board membership, and/or volunteerism).
· Thinks strategically and has demonstrated experience leading organizational growth, managed change, and driving strategic planning processes that produce measurable results.
· Serves as the organization's chief fundraiser, with a demonstrated track record in major gifts, foundation relations, corporate partnerships, grant procurement, and revenue diversification across multiple funding streams.
· Serves as a visible public ambassador for Brooke's Place, telling the organization's story compellingly to boards, funders, media, policymakers, and the public, while actively advancing advocacy efforts around critical childhood grief programming.
· Holds high standards of fairness, transparency, integrity and accountability.
· Possesses a strong financial acumen and exercises disciplined financial stewardship, with the ability to oversee budgets, manage risk, and make sound resource allocation decisions that keep the mission and the bottom line in balance.
· Carries a genuine commitment to helping grieving children and families to thrive in the midst of grief.
· Believes, as a daily practice, that every grieving child deserves to feel safe, supported and understood in their grief journey.
· Brings a practical, engaged leadership style and is willing to roll up their sleeves alongside staff, volunteers, and board members to meet the needs of the organization and the families it serves.
· Leads, motivates, and develops a dedicated team, supporting staff in carrying out their respective roles with clarity, purpose, and a culture of shared values and belonging.

Qualifications

· Brings eight to ten or more years of proven leadership experience in nonprofit sector (through employment, board membership, and/or volunteerism).
· Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, public administration, business, social services, or a related field is required. Equivalent relevant education and experience will be considered.
· A master's degree in nonprofit management, public administration, business, counseling, social work, or a related field is preferred.
· Experience growing a smaller nonprofit or mission-based organization is preferred.
· Knowledge of Central Indiana and relationships across its nonprofit, civic, philanthropic, healthcare, or business communities are advantageous.
Compensation and Benefits
· Brooke's Place offers competitive compensation, including a salary range beginning at $120K, commensurate with the candidate's relevant experience and qualifications.
· Benefits include healthcare reimbursement; dental and vision coverage; a SIMPLE IRA retirement plan; flexible work arrangements; and paid time off, including holidays, sick time, and vacation time.

The Chief Program Officer is a senior executive who will translate Future Caucus' strategy into a coherent, high-impact experience for lawmakers across their full lifecycle in the network. They ensure the experience for our lawmakers delivers measurable results against our mission and long-term outcomes, manage a team responsible for executing exceptional programming, and represent Future Caucus' programmatic strategy and impact to external audiences.

The CPO will establish a clear bar for what excellent programming looks like and develop the judgement and leadership of their team to execute against that bar. They ensure strong organizational learning cycles about our programs to guide programmatic decision-making. As a key member of the executive team, they work closely with the President & CEO and other senior leaders to facilitate cohesion between programmatic and other organizational outcomes, and advise the executive team on threats, opportunities, and new initiatives that advance the ability of young legislators to govern effectively and wield their political power.

The CPO will focus on strategic sustainable growth for Future Caucus programming - and will serve as an external representative of Future Caucus' CEO at functions, to funders, and the media. They oversee a team responsible for executing a portfolio that includes 1) strategic planning implementation; 2) the lawmaker-engagement lifecycle from recruitment of new members to the Future Caucus network through alumnihood; 3) lawmaker-facing cross-state programming and state chapter success; and 5) program evaluation & learning. They will ensure a team-wide dedication to rigorous relationship management and data tracking, seamless internal communications, and collaborative cross-team relationships.

We're looking for someone who is excited about joining a team during a period of organizational growth and loves flexing their skill of helping a team translate visionary-level thinking into exemplary day-to-day execution.

The ideal candidate has significant experience developing other leaders and relishes taking on the role of player-coach as they help others grow. They also have a deep understanding of the realities facing elected officials, especially at the state level, and can align programming around their anticipation of what young lawmakers will need to govern effectively. They are eager to bring an entrepreneurial spirit to their work, knowing that transforming American politics will take disruptive and innovative thinking from them and their entire team. Critically, they have a sincere commitment to working across partisan lines to define the next era of leadership in America.

About Future Caucus

Future Caucus has an audacious mission: activate young leaders to bridge the partisan divide and transform American politics. Future Caucus is a national, nonpartisan organization dedicated to supporting the next generation of elected leaders. We provide the resources, networking, and capacity-building opportunities for these policymakers to forge productive partnerships on critical national issues.

In 2013, Future Caucus organized the nation's first and only caucus for young members of Congress, the Congressional Future Caucus, to build coalitions on future-oriented challenges. Future Caucus also scaled this model into 36 state legislatures, each with a Future Caucus consisting of young, high-potential legislators, and now engages more than 2,100 young legislators nationwide. In 2025, Future Caucus' President & CEO was named to the TIME100 Next list. Learn more at www.futurecaucus.org.

Responsibilities

Leadership, Management, and Coaching

The CPO is first and foremost a leader of leaders. A strong orientation to and track record of leading toward results through layers is required for the role.

Supervise, coach & lead a group of program leaders and their direct reports; operating as a multiplier who seeks to unlock the intelligence and potential of all team members
Create and implement information sharing streams across legislator-facing teams that enable more strategic decision making, communication, and cooperation
Model and establish an effective feedback and learning culture across the program team, contributing to a staff-wide living of our organizational values
Set performance goals and accountability systems to build a culture of results-based leadership
Shape and clarify emerging roles, teams, and operating models as Future Caucus grows, working with the senior leadership team to ensure each team member has what they need to do some of the best work of their lives
Develop a team-based environment to motivate and inspire staff to work collaboratively toward vision and goals
Organize work allocation & project management, training, problem resolution, and performance evaluation for your direct reports, and support your direct reports in doing so for their teams
Support the development and management of budgets across all programmatic activities and initiatives, in collaboration with the senior leadership team

Programmatic Strategy & Execution

The CPO's mandate is to develop and oversee execution of Future Caucus' lawmaker programming strategy to achieve our vision and long-term outcomes.

Translate Future Caucus' organizational strategy into clear programmatic priorities, goals, outcomes, and measures of success for the program team
Manage the design & oversee the execution of a strategy for the ideal Future Caucus member lifecycle, from identifying and recruiting prospective members, to onboarding and ongoing engagement, to an "alumni" transition
Monitor emerging needs and interests among key stakeholders such as legislators, partner organizations, and funders, partnering with the executive team to turn field insights into tangible organizational action
Build and execute clear programmatic learning cycles that enable your team to 1) monitor progress to goals; 2) analyze data & adjust to emerging trends; and 3) inform programmatic strategy
Ensure the state chapter model and cross-state programming model work in concert with one another, leading to real outcomes for chapters & lawmakers as a result of the synthesis of deep relationship building, powerful leadership training, innovative policy solutions, and robust press coverage
Lead program input into strategic and annual planning, ensuring alignment to organizational priorities
Support program directors in developing and strengthening strategic partnerships, ensuring the partnerships align with organizational need and enhance organizational strategy
Create and manage accountability systems so that relationship management data is captured in organizational CRM systems across the program team

Executive Leadership

The CPO sits on the executive team, which is tasked with ensuring the long-term future of the organization, making strategic decisions about resource allocation, and executing against Future Caucus' vision cohesively. All members of the executive team:

Think 2-4 years ahead for the entire organization & your teams, looking around the corner to identify strengths, opportunities, threats & weaknesses that the organization should act on
Represent Future Caucus's programmatic strategy, quality, and impact with credibility before funders, partners, policymakers, and other high-level external audiences
Provide leadership within & thought partnership to the executive team on organizational priorities, work planning, team coordination, and team culture
Participate in quarterly Board of Directors meetings, sharing relevant updates and integrating insights or feedback back into Future Caucus efforts
Collaborate with the Development department to align grant proposals and reports to organizational priorities, making certain that grant requirements are met through programmatic execution and achievements

Administration & Miscellaneous

Any job comes with its fair share of administrative tasks, including this one. Things like systems upkeep, expense reporting, data entry, and grant reporting, etc
Perform other related duties as needed

Requirements

ABOUT YOU

Required 10+ years of relevant experience; at least 4 years of experience managing senior leaders and multidisciplinary teams across multiple programs on team sizes of 5+
Track record of leading teams to achieve more than they thought possible through strong staff development, coaching & leadership
Political savvy - you have In-depth familiarity with state-level politics and the day to day governing needs of young lawmakers
A known dot-connector who is more motivated by getting things right than by being right
Natural relationship builder with a knack for network building
Comfortable speaking publicly on behalf of Future Caucus to VIP rooms
Creative, entrepreneurial, and self-motivated
Has a high bar for excellence and an ability to motivate others to achieve it
Detail-oriented and proactive communicator, not only skilled at managing those who report to you, but managing up laterally

OUR VALUES

In 2020, Future Caucus unveiled a set of organizational value statements developed collaboratively by our team. This ethos represents what we believe in at Future Caucus, and what we have worked to establish during the last eleven years. These are the values we have set for ourselves, and what we see come to life through our legislators in our network, partners, and supporters:

Listen First: communicate openly and respectfully - make room for others at the table
Say "We": there is no "I" in Future Caucus - welcome diversity; it makes us stronger
Build Trust: Integrity in our relationships is fundamental - be reliable and follow through
Empower Others: Be empathetic - practice transparency and collaborate openly
Break Barriers: Climb it, go through it, or work around it - limits are challenges to overcome
Innovate Freely: Disruption leads to creative solutions - forge a new path forward

Benefits

LOCATION

Future Caucus is currently in a hybrid work environment, with staff coming in 3 days per week every other week. Ideal candidates must be located in the Washington, D.C. metro area, or be willing to relocate.

Compensation

Salary for this position is $151,000-$163,000
and the position is bonus eligible. Highly competitive benefits are provided, including commuter/telework stipend, 401(k) with employer contributions, generous vacation policy, professional development stipend, and comprehensive health benefits.

CULTURE AND CONNECTION

Future Caucus aspires to an organizational culture based on our values, where our team is connected and collaborative. We take time to share in the wins and impact of our work, chat over regular employer-paid lunches, learn together, and participate in local social and service activities. We are eager to add team members who share our values and will continue building our positive culture.

HIRING PROCESS

The priority deadline for this role is Oct. 26, 2026
and we anticipate communicating to all candidates following our priority deadline. Applications received after this date will be evaluated on a rolling basis.

Additional Information

As an equal opportunity employer, Future Caucus is committed to a diverse and inclusive work environment. We welcome members of historically underrepresented groups to apply, including people of color, women, LGBTQ+ individuals, veterans, individuals with disabilities, and multilingual individuals. Reference checks are conducted on all prospective new hires.

About This Opportunity

Working closely with and reporting to the Vice Provost for Enrollment Management, the Executive Director assists with the development and implementation of enrollment-related strategies, policies and initiatives in order to realize University enrollment goals and desired outcomes. This position plays a key role in advancing the UW’s 2026–2030 Strategic Framework, including its commitments to a high-quality, debt-free education, unlocking opportunity, operational excellence, workforce development and Working as One UW.

The Executive Director provides innovative and strategic vision, leadership and operations management in the administration of all federal, state, institutional and private financial aid and scholarship programs for all three UW campuses. The Executive Director manages approximately 32 FTE within the Office of Student Financial Aid, which includes Veterans Education Benefits Office and Childcare Assistance Program. Responsible for a financial aid program of $800 million for approximately 33,000 students, the Executive Director oversees the planning, organizing and directing of all services provided by these units. In light of institutional mission and enrollment goals, the Executive Director both integrates and ensures compliance with federal, state, institutional and private aid rules and regulations. In collaboration with the Vice Provost and the Enrollment Management leadership team, the Executive Director exercises strategic leadership in the development and implementation of institutional policies regarding the evaluation of financial need and the packaging of aid in order to realize University enrollment goals, including access for and retention of a diverse student population. Serve as the primary liaison between the University and various federal, state and local agencies providing financial aid to students

Provide recommendations on strategy and implementation of institutional policies for evaluation of financial need and packaging of aid using data and assessment.
Provide strategic leadership for UW scholarship strategy, including the coordination, administration, and evaluation of institutional and donor-funded scholarship programs.

Perform duties as NCAA UW designated financial aid authority and work with Intercollegiate Athletics on athletic scholarship issues and eligibility decisions

NEXCOM CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER

NF-06 / SES-Equivalent

This position is located in the Navy Exchange Service Command (NEXCOM),
an Echelon III command within the Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Enterprise.

NEXCOM’s mission is to provide authorized customers with quality goods and services at a savings while enabling warfighter readiness and supporting Navy quality-of-life programs for Sailors, military families, retirees, veterans, and other authorized patrons worldwide. The incumbent serves as NEXCOM’s Director/Chief Executive Officer and exercises full responsibility for the strategic direction, management, and oversight of the worldwide NEXCOM Enterprise. This includes providing executive leadership for Navy Exchange retail and services, the NEXCOM Hospitality Group, the Ship’s Store Program, the Uniform Program Management Office, the Navy Clothing and Textile Research Facility, and the Telecommunications Program Office.

The incumbent directs a geographically dispersed workforce of approximately 13,000 associates operating on 100+ naval bases worldwide, including locations in 13 foreign countries, and is responsible for aligning NEXCOM’s strategy and operations with NAVSUP, Department of the Navy, Department of War, and Chief of Naval Operations priorities.

The CEO also oversees significant non-appropriated and appropriated fund resources, capital investments, employee benefit assets, and funds generated to support Navy quality-of-life programs. NEXCOM generates more than $3 billion in annual revenue, and the CEO is accountable for the operational performance, financial integrity, modernization, and long-term sustainability of the enterprise.

 In-depth mastery and experience of planning, organizational development, engineering management, system development, and systems engineering.
 Ability to lead complex systems development and support programs involving interaction with a variety of organizations, laboratories, field activities, and contractors.
 Ability to lead the evaluation and incorporation of new technology into technical plans, proposals, and specifications governing subsequent systems design, development, production, procurement, and utilization.

Job Summary:
The incumbent serves as the Director/Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Navy Exchange Service Command (NEXCOM). The NEXCOM CEO exercises complete responsibility for the strategic direction, management, fiduciary, and technical control of all NEXCOM Programs, which consist of Navy Exchanges (NEXs), NEXCOM Hospitality Group (NHG) Lodging, Ship's Stores, Navy Uniform Program, Navy Clothing and Textile Research Facility, and Navy Personal Telecommunications Program Office. The Programs managed by NEXCOM represent a major non-pay element of DoW's total compensation system. They are major quality-of-life benefits for DoW active duty and retired military, dependents, DoW civilians, and other authorized patrons. The mission of the Navy Exchange Service Command is to provide quality goods and services at a savings and to support Navy Quality of Life Programs. Responsibilities are global in scope. It involves the management and operation of a world-wide system of 100+ retail and hospitality complexes consisting of: 250+ retail stores; over 1000 service outlets; over 600 contracted and direct run food service outlets; 96 uniform shops, 141 Ships Stores afloat and ashore; 115 Micro Markets; 95 Navy Lodges and Navy Inns with over 17,000 beds; and other support facilities, employing approximately 13,000 U.S. citizen, local national employees and military personnel with over $3 billion in annual revenues. NEXCOM also provides direct fleet support, managing uniform inventory and reclaim operations at Navy Recruit Training Command, providing housing rental payment services for the AUKUS initiative, and responding to Fleet and Regional Commander requests in crisis and contingency operations.

Duties And Responsibilities:

Through subordinate Command senior executives (5 of whom are at the NF6 grade level) and 2 senior military personnel (06/05 level), and in close coordination with senior Navy and DoN/DoW leadership, the NEXCOM CEO is accountable for programmatic direction, oversight, and successful delivery of all NEXCOM non-appropriated and appropriated fund programs worldwide, which encompass annual revenues of about $3 billion. Responsible for optimizing business processes and institutionalizing performance standards throughout the Command to improve operating plans and standards and ensure optimum efficiency. Incorporate innovative and evolving concepts and trends into the Command's business practices.
Establish system-wide policies and strategic direction that are aligned with higher echelon strategic objectives and priorities. Serves as the proponent for the strategic corporate mission and serves as NEXCOM's primary representative to many key groups that have an interest in NEXCOM's six business lines, including the Congress, military chain of command including Secretary of War, Secretary of Navy, Chief of Naval Operations, Naval Supply Systems Command, external organizations, corporate business officials, and representatives of public organizations.
Manages changes in policymaking and program planning and provides command and control over NEXCOM's organization. Ensures strong corporate internal controls that safeguard assets, support accurate financial reporting, and maintain compliance with regulatory standards, directly contributing to achieving clean financial audits and fostering a culture of transparency and accountability.
Exercises fiduciary responsibility for non-appropriated fund investments of approximately $2 billion, pension plan assets of over $1.8 billion, and employee 401(k) plan assets of over $520M. Oversees development and execution of appropriated fund requirements of approximately $120M in support of NAF and Uniform R&D programs.
Establishes annual NEX program operating budgets and profit forecasts to be used in the development of Morale, Welfare and Recreation (MWR) profit distribution plans.
Establishes annual and long-range NEX capital investment programs for Navy MWR/NEX Board of Directors approval.
Establishes annual program operating budgets and annual and long-range capital investment programs for NEXCOM Hospitality Group.
As a DON NAF Component Head, formulate, coordinate, interpret, and appraise civilian personnel policies and procedures and exercise general supervision over the entire Human Resources Program. Plan, develop, review, and establish policies to achieve an optimum Human Resources Program for NEXCOM and field activities.
Exercise centralized control over the hiring, career development, promotion, placement, training, and performance appraisal of all managers throughout NEXCOM Enterprise. Develop training programs for all elements and levels of the Enterprise to ensure effective mission accomplishment.
Procure equipment, merchandise, services, and supplies; develop and monitor purchasing policies and procedures.
Possesses inherent procurement authority using NAF. Establishes and promulgates uniform policies, procedures, and instructions for the procurement of goods, services (including concessions and other revenue-generating services), construction, and resale items.
Develop merchandising techniques and operational controls. Conduct quality tests and evaluations to improve merchandise offerings and operational techniques.
Manage and establish operating policies and procedures for the Ships Stores Program, administer Ships Store Profits, Navy (SSPN) General Fund (GF); provide and maintain adequate reserves for Navy Exchange and NEXCOM Hospitality Group facilities; provide for insurance and Fidelity bonds; replacement of major equipment, standard forms and other benefits for the Navy Exchange and NEXCOM Hospitality Group Programs.
Develops and implements practices which will promote employee morale and resolve problems of employee relations and/or complaints. We ensure equal employment opportunity for all employees and job applicants, and that principles of fairness, equity, and transparency permeate the Command.

CONTROLS OVER POSITION

The NEXCOM CEO reports to the Commander, Naval Supply Systems Command (COMNAVSUPSYSCOM). NEXCOM strategic objectives are developed to align and support strategies developed by DoW, SECNAV, CNO, and COMNAVSUPSYSCOM. The CEO reports to and is accountable to the MWR/NEX Board of Directors, which provides strategic direction for NEX and MWR programs, sets financial goals and objectives, determines profit-sharing formulas, and conducts periodic reviews of operating results. The CEO uses exceptional initiative and ingenuity to direct NEXCOM operations. Performance is evaluated in terms of results achieved and effectiveness in accomplishment of the mission. The CEO provides annual reports to the DASW (MC&FP) and testifies at Congressional proceedings as called.

Must be a U.S. citizen able to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance.

ORGANIZATION OVERVIEW

The Seattle Social Housing Developer (SSHD) is a Public Development Authority (PDA) committed to creating, owning, and stewarding permanently affordable, mixed-income social housing that is publicly financed, publicly controlled, and free from market speculation. As we lay the foundation for this transformative model, guided by international examples and rooted in public accountability, we are building a team to define a new standard for equitable, sustainable, and community-centered social housing development in Seattle. Our goal is to expand access, strengthen the social fabric of our city, and ensure housing that is affordable forever and inclusive by design for current and future generations.

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Director of Operations reports directly to the Chief Operating Officer and converts SSHD’s operational strategy into consistent, accountable execution. The Director builds the operating routines, tools, workflows, and cross-functional coordination needed to support a growing portfolio, implement the social housing model, prepare for property acquisitions and transitions, and ensure that commitments move from decision to completion. 

This is a hands-on leadership role for an operator who can establish structure in a rapidly evolving public development organization. The Director does not replace the COO’s enterprise leadership or the day-to-day responsibilities of third-party property management, asset management, finance, compliance, resident governance, communications, human resources, information technology, or real estate development. The Director connects those functions, manages implementation, identifies gaps, and escalates matters requiring executive judgment.

POSITION DETAILS

Job Title:
Director of Operations
Department:
Operations
Reports To:
Chief Operating Officer
Direct Reports:
Yes
FLSA Status:
Exempt
Pay:
$145,000 - $185,000

SCOPE OF AUTHORITY & ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIONSHIPS

The COO sets enterprise direction and remains accountable for organizational performance. The Director of Operations owns the management discipline that turns that direction into coordinated execution.
Internal: Chief Operating Officer; Interim CEO; CFO; Chief Real Estate Development Officer; future CIO; Director of Real Estate and Governance; Communications; Asset Management; Compliance; Human Resources; Finance; resident governance staff; and administrative staff. 
External: third-party property managers; legal counsel; operational, compliance, asset-management, resident-governance, and other consultants; security and facilities vendors; community partners; and public-agency counterparts as delegated.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Operational Infrastructure and Management Systems 

Develop and maintain SSHD’s operational calendar, annual work plan, decision log, policy inventory, standard operating procedure library, and implementation trackers. 
Establish clear operating rhythms, including cross-functional meetings, dashboards, action-item ownership, deadlines, escalation protocols, and executive follow-up. 
Translate approved policies and executive decisions into workflows, templates, training, controls, and measurable deliverables. 
Identify process gaps, duplicated work, unclear ownership, and operational risks; recommend and implement practical improvements. 
Support implementation and adoption of enterprise work-management and information systems in partnership with the COO and future CIO; serve as a business-process owner rather than the technology owner.

Portfolio Growth and Acquisition Readiness 

Lead the operating-readiness workstream for acquisitions, new developments, property transitions, and lease-up activities after strategic direction and transaction parameters are approved. 
Maintain integrated readiness plans covering property-management onboarding, staffing, vendor mobilization, resident communications, compliance, leasing and waitlist workflows, building operations, security, emergency preparedness, insurance coordination, and opening-day requirements. 
Coordinate owners, consultants, property managers, and internal departments, so operational dependencies are surfaced early and completed on schedule. 
Facilitate post-acquisition and post-launch reviews and ensure lessons learned are incorporated into future playbooks. 
Support the long-term evaluation and stand-up of internal property-management capacity while preserving clear accountability for current third-party property managers. 

Property Management and Vendor Coordination 

Monitor third-party property-management compliance with approved work plans, service expectations, reporting requirements, management agreements, and escalation protocols; route performance concerns to the COO and Asset Management. 
Coordinate recurring property operations reviews and maintain follow-up on occupancy, delinquency, work orders, incidents, security, resident communications, building conditions, and other operating indicators. 
Track high-priority incidents and corrective actions across property management, vendors, counsel, insurance, communications, and internal staff while preserving the decision rights of the accountable function. 
Support vendor scopes, procurements, onboarding, performance monitoring, renewals, and closeout in partnership with Finance and the designated procurement lead. 
Ensure vendor and consultant deliverables are integrated into SSHD operations rather than remaining stand-alone reports or recommendations. 

Social Housing Program Implementation

Coordinate implementation of the approved social housing operating model, including resident-facing materials, internal playbooks, affordability progression processes, internal and external waitlist administration, eligibility workflows, and staff training. 
Partner with Compliance, Asset Management, Finance, Resident Governance, Communications, legal counsel, and property management to operationalize approved program rules. 
Maintain implementation controls, readiness checklists, exception-routing procedures, and records showing how policies are being applied. 
Track operational impacts and patterns and elevate policy questions, financial tradeoffs, resident impacts, or legal risks that require COO or executive-team decisions. 
Support consistent implementation of resident services referrals, restorative-justice processes, resident governance commitments, and housing-stability procedures without assuming the technical ownership of those functions. 

Organizational Operations 

Oversee coordinated day-to-day administrative operations, including office operations, shared operational calendars, records and workflow management, business continuity, and cross-department logistics. 
Partner with Human Resources on onboarding and offboarding operations, role clarity, training logistics, and implementation of organizational policies. 
Partner with Finance on purchasing workflows, invoice and contract routing, budget tracking for assigned operating initiatives, and internal controls. 
Coordinate emergency-response and continuity plans and help ensure staff understand roles, escalation paths, and documentation expectations. 
Supervise and develop operations staff, establish service standards, and build capacity that can scale with portfolio and headcount growth.

Performance, Risk, and Executive Support 

Prepare concise operational dashboards and decision-ready briefing materials for the COO, executive team, and, as requested, the Interim CEO or Board. 
Maintain an enterprise operational risk and dependency log and ensure responsible leaders act on mitigation plans. 
Distinguish routine operational issues from matters requiring legal, financial, policy, reputational, resident-impact, or executive review and escalate promptly. 
Analyze operating data and trends, recommend corrective action, and verify that approved corrective actions are completed. 
Serve as the COO’s delegate on implementation matters within defined authority; do not make policy, financial, personnel, legal, or external commitments beyond delegated authority.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND ABILITIES

Demonstrated ability to build operational systems, standard operating procedures, accountability structures, and performance dashboards in a growing or changing organization. 
Experience coordinating multiple departments, vendors, consultants, and executive stakeholders around time-sensitive deliverables. 
Strong judgment regarding escalation, decision rights, confidentiality, resident impact, and organizational risk. 
Excellent project management, written communication, meeting facilitation, analytical, and follow-through skills. 
Ability to organize incomplete information, clarify ownership, and move work forward without overstepping functional expertise or delegated authority. 
Commitment to racial equity, public accountability, housing stability, resident dignity, and SSHD’s social housing mission.

The Opportunity

Few childhood events are as life-altering as the death of a parent, sibling, or significant person. Since 1999, Brooke's Place has helped change the lives of grieving children and families through peer support groups, therapy services, camp-based programming, and community education. With the retirement of a long-time Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Brooke's Place is seeking a mission-centered, people-oriented leader who will preserve the organization's warmth and clinical integrity while preparing it for responsible growth.
Brooke's Place is the only organization providing ongoing grief services specifically for children and families in Central Indiana. Poised for continued growth, we seek an inspiring and experienced leader who can build on a strong foundation of committed donors, volunteers, staff, and community partners. The next CEO will bring strong communication and relationship-building skills, sound business judgment, emotional intelligence, and the ability to translate vision into sustainable results without losing sight of the mission.

What and Who You'll Lead

As CEO, the selected candidate will be responsible for the overall leadership and management of Brooke's Place organization, including but not limited to: community and public relations, fundraising; development and cultivation of donors, program service models and expansion; human resources management, grant-writing oversight; financial management and compliance; Board of Directors administration and support; and legal, tax, risk and facilities management. Three of the 15 staff members report directly to this individual, who reports to the Brooke's Place Board of Directors.

The CEO will partner closely with the Board on strategic direction, fund development, and organizational priorities. Working in partnership with clinical and functional leaders, the CEO will strengthen the people, systems, partnerships, and infrastructure needed to expand impact while protecting program quality and organizational culture.
The role also requires visible and flexible leadership of a mission-driven team whose programs, volunteer activities, donor events, and family needs may extend beyond traditional business hours.

Key Priorities for the First 12 Months

· Build trust with staff, board, donors, and community partners through presence, transparency, and consistent follow-through, establishing relationships with deeply passionate volunteers, staff, and donors.
· Collaborate with the Clinical Programs Director and program team to assess the current state of programs and operations, assessing whether the model is right-sized and right-shaped for current demand, future growth, geographic reach, and long-term organizational sustainability.
· Work with the Advancement Director and team to strengthen financial systems, stewardship practices, and development infrastructure, with meaningful progress toward new major gift relationships, corporate partnerships, planned giving efforts, and a diversified revenue base.
· Evaluate the facilities, technology, data, staffing, and operating capabilities needed for the organization's next phase.
· Deepen referral and community partnerships across schools, healthcare, hospice, funeral service, nonprofit, civic, and business networks.
· Improve the use of outcomes and evaluation to demonstrate impact, inform decisions, and support fundraising.
· Foster a culture in which staff and volunteers feel supported, valued, accountable, and equipped to succeed.

Who We're Looking For

Brooke's Place seeks a leader first, with genuine passion for this mission. The ideal candidate:
· Brings eight to ten or more years of proven senior leadership, preferably in the nonprofit sector (through employment, board membership, and/or volunteerism).
· Thinks strategically and has demonstrated experience leading organizational growth, managed change, and driving strategic planning processes that produce measurable results.
· Serves as the organization's chief fundraiser, with a demonstrated track record in major gifts, foundation relations, corporate partnerships, grant procurement, and revenue diversification across multiple funding streams.
· Serves as a visible public ambassador for Brooke's Place, telling the organization's story compellingly to boards, funders, media, policymakers, and the public, while actively advancing advocacy efforts around critical childhood grief programming.
· Holds high standards of fairness, transparency, integrity and accountability.
· Possesses a strong financial acumen and exercises disciplined financial stewardship, with the ability to oversee budgets, manage risk, and make sound resource allocation decisions that keep the mission and the bottom line in balance.
· Carries a genuine commitment to helping grieving children and families to thrive in the midst of grief.
· Believes, as a daily practice, that every grieving child deserves to feel safe, supported and understood in their grief journey.
· Brings a practical, engaged leadership style and is willing to roll up their sleeves alongside staff, volunteers, and board members to meet the needs of the organization and the families it serves.
· Leads, motivates, and develops a dedicated team, supporting staff in carrying out their respective roles with clarity, purpose, and a culture of shared values and belonging.

Qualifications

· Brings eight to ten or more years of proven leadership experience in nonprofit sector (through employment, board membership, and/or volunteerism).
· Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, public administration, business, social services, or a related field is required. Equivalent relevant education and experience will be considered.
· A master's degree in nonprofit management, public administration, business, counseling, social work, or a related field is preferred.
· Experience growing a smaller nonprofit or mission-based organization is preferred.
· Knowledge of Central Indiana and relationships across its nonprofit, civic, philanthropic, healthcare, or business communities are advantageous.
Compensation and Benefits
· Brooke's Place offers competitive compensation, including a salary range beginning at $120K, commensurate with the candidate's relevant experience and qualifications.
· Benefits include healthcare reimbursement; dental and vision coverage; a SIMPLE IRA retirement plan; flexible work arrangements; and paid time off, including holidays, sick time, and vacation time.

Position
: Chief Program Officer

Position Type
: Full-Time

Reports to
: Layla Zaidane, President & CEO
